I've farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father grew wheat and corn here, and I do the same. I know this soil — it's flat, decent, but dry. The rainfall never comes when you need it, so I rely on the well.

At my age, I'm not trying anything risky. My two sons moved to the city years ago. It's mostly just me and my wife working the fields. I manage about 10 mu. The land is registered to me and I know every corner of it.

**Wheat** was planted last October as always. Right now in April it's at jointing stage. I already put down the base fertilizer before planting and did the pre-winter irrigation. Now I'll topdress with urea at jointing and make sure it gets water at heading and grain filling. I spray for aphids and rust when I see them — happened twice last year. I use the Jimai-22 variety the village supply shop sells. It performs steadily. I'll harvest in late June.

**Corn** goes into the same ground right after wheat comes off, no-till now — the township extension station pushed this a few years back and my neighbor tried it first, so I followed. I use a Zhengdan-958 hybrid bag, same as always. Summer rain helps but I irrigate once if August runs dry. I apply fertilizer twice — at planting and at knee-high stage.

I don't experiment. I do what works.
